item.description: 03:41 PM EDT, 08/31/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Consumer stocks were lower late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (
item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:41 PM EDT, 08/31/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Consumer stocks were lower late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) falling 0.5% and the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) decreasing 0.6%. In corporate news, Toyota (TM) and Honda (HMC) could get stuck with the bill if President Trump's 50% tariff on Canadian car imports go into effect on Jan. 1 as proposed, Reuters reported. Toyota and Honda could be forced to shut down some production lines, according to the late Sunday report, which cited analysts. If the tariffs go into effect, the two automakers will likely try to redirect vehicles built in Canada to other markets and look for ways to make up supply for the US market, analysts told the media outlet. Toyota shares were up 1%, and Honda was adding 0.3%.

item.description: 03:29 PM EDT, 08/31/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were lower in late Monday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index and the State Street
item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:29 PM EDT, 08/31/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were lower in late Monday afternoon trading, with the NYSE Financial Index and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) each shedding 0.6%. The Philadelphia Housing Index was falling 1.8%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) decreased 0.6%. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was increasing 1.8% to $79,059, and the yield for 10-year US Treasuries rose 3.8 basis points to 4.758%. In corporate news, UBS (UBS) can meet 50% of its new capital requirements with debt, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing a recommendation from the upper house of the Swiss parliament's Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee. Specifically, the panel recommended that UBS be allowed to meet half of the new requirements with convertible AT1 debt rather than the highest-quality equity, according to the news outlet. UBS shares were up 1.7%.

item.title: ReGen III management cites Middle East-driven Group III base oil supply disruptions as key factor in 2Q 2026 commentary
item.description: In management commentary for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, ReGen III cited progress in validating its used motor oil re-refining technology.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In management commentary for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, ReGen III cited progress in validating its used motor oil re-refining technology. The three-stage process targets Group III base oil output from molecular separation, with Group II/II+ produced via hydro-treatment of a lower-quality stream. Management pointed to pilot operations at 5 bpd over several thousand hours, with Group III output meeting API specifications. Independent and third-party engineering work was cited as supporting feasibility, yields, and energy efficiency versus conventional re-refining approaches. Management tied market conditions to 2026 supply disruptions, citing reliance on imports and pricing volatility as demand support for domestic Group III supply.
